features.name: first_person_share_oc
features.definition: What proportion of words across the counter-argument comments are first-person singular pronouns (I, me, my)?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments with json.loads into a list of strings; if missing or malformed return null. Concatenate all comments. Tokenize words with re.findall(r"[A-Za-z']+", text.lower()). Count tokens in {'i','me','my'} (also count contractions I'm, I've, I'll, I'd as 'i' by tokens starting with "i'" ; exclude 'mine','myself'). Return count / total word tokens. Empty list or zero words returns null.

h0: first_person_share_oc has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view.
h1: Lower first_person_share_oc is associated with a higher probability of view change (negative coefficient).
note: Operational assumption: first-person language is measured as share of I/me/my words (with I-contractions) pooled across all counter-comments; list order carries no meaning. The parenthetical 'less anecdotal' is only the rationale; anecdotes are not measured separately. Raw text may include quoted text from others or OP-change announcements (contamination/timing risk), and no comment timing is supplied. Association only, not causal.
